2_Introduction: The control device displays a JSC of 23.29 mA/cm², a VOC of 1.0852 V and an FF of 66.45%, tuning out a PCE of 16.79%. The perovskite solution (1.73 mol/L) was prepared according to chemical formula of Cs0.05MA0.16FA0.79Pb1I2.9Br0.1. Spin-coating was conducted in two stages: 1000 rpm for 10 s, then 5000 rpm for 30 s. The carefully timed introduction of 160 µL antisolvent at last 6 s played a crucial role in controlling film morphology. The substrate was then transferred to a thermostatic heater and annealed at 110 °C for 25 min. XRD analysis showed a diffraction peak was identified at 4.00°, with an intensity of 0.00 cts，which corresponds to the formation of a 2D structure within the perovskite lattice. The high intensity implies efficient surface passivation, contributing positively to device performance. GIXRD analysis further revealed a residual tensile stress of 22.50 MPa in the perovskite film via measurement conducted at an incident angle of 1°.
3_Result_Discussion: The triple-cation mixed-halide perovskite Cs0.05MA0.16FA0.79Pb1I2.9Br0.1, processed from a high-concentration precursor via a two-stage spin-coating protocol with a precisely timed antisolvent drip, undergoes rapid nucleation and dense film formation, where the subsequent thermal annealing at 110 °C facilitates grain growth and reduces bulk defect density, thereby mitigating non-radiative recombination pathways. The crystallographic analysis via XRD reveals the formation of a low-dimensional phase, evidenced by a distinct peak at 4.00°, which signifies the incorporation of a 2D structure within the 3D lattice that effectively passivates grain boundaries and interfaces, suppressing charge carrier trapping. Furthermore, grazing-incidence XRD quantifies a residual tensile stress of 22.50 MPa within the film, a state that, while potentially influencing ion migration kinetics, is concurrently mitigated by the stabilizing presence of the in-situ formed 2D phase, which collectively enhances structural order and interfacial charge extraction. This synergistic interplay between optimized crystallization kinetics, passivating low-dimensional phase integration, and managed film stress culminates in improved photovoltaic parameters, yielding a JSC of 23.29 mA/cm², a VOC of 1.0852 V, an FF of 66.45%, and a final PCE of 16.79%.
